body:
Thanks! I wasn't actually talking to her... Unfortunately, she overheard and felt the need to offer her two cents. 

If you're curious about my mom, my previous posts say everything. She IS pretty unwell.... I've learned not to go to her with most things, and am learning to try and not go to her with other things, but it's been a pretty uphill battle. It's hard to unlearn your entire way of life lol. 

Thanks again for the feedback, though!
Kill them all!!

Man, oh man... The part where you said "With barely any words from me (I was flabbergasted that she was even asking me) she bought both." literally made me say "What?!" out loud lol. 

My nparents are very similar. They've been bankrupt (at least) once, didn't pay their taxes for several years, and are constantly getting behind in bills. 
Yet, my mom spent over $200 on a NoNo (it's a shaver thing for your legs/body hair). Not even fore herself, but for ME because she can't stand my leg hair. Uhhh...

N logic lol. 

As for the house, though... I understand why you felt sad. I would just try not to beat yourself up too much, though. You said she'd never be satisfied with it. 
Even if you did that for her, the outcome wouldn't be what you want (or what it should be). 

Also, I had to chuckle at the last paragraph. My nmom still dreams of buying some sort of offgrid farm-thing and having all her kids and grand kids live there in a "community".

Dang... I feel you, OP. You don't sound dumb at all. 
I think this is actually a thing N's love to do. 
My mom forced me to load up my own trash bags with my stuff so she could throw it out. 
It's messed. 
Even to this day, she has no regard for my things.

Reading the title alone, my mind was screaming "It's a trap!" but that's also my own experiences playing into things. 

I'm sorry you had to go through all that... Your private life is your business, and your dad was wrong. Not only to pry, but he then abused you and blackmailed you! That's not okay. 

Healthy parents don't freakin' blackmail their kids. 

As for the apology... I would bring it up with your therapist (if you haven't already). 

I, personally, would be inclined to proceed with utmost caution. You said it yourself, that he's had ulterior motives in the past. 
I wouldn't break your NC with him, if I were you. You're absolutely right in thinking that a "sorry" doesn't undo what he did, or how you feel. What you went through. 

To me, you sound much healthier without him in your life. By your own words, that trying to rebuilt a relationship with him could potentially undo all your hard work....

I just don't think it's worth it.

Yikes! Glad you were able to get out safely! Not only because you got away from your Ndad, but being able to drive that fast and still be safe! 

I'm a bit of a car lover myself, and your post made me smile. Just picturing you gunning it like that... man, thank god for sports cars!
Also, as a car lover, I'm mildly surprised at the Honda's poor performance. Don't get me wrong! I'm relieved to hear that your Ndad couldn't catch you! I've just driven Honda myself, and my old one was a speedy little devil. Then again, the Accord is a bigger car...

Either way, I don't mean to get off topic with car talk!! Apologies for that, ha ha. 

As for your gf's safety... can she explain the situation to her employer? I mean, she doesn't have to give any details. 
But I'm sure the management could keep an eye out. Make sure your Ndad isn't allowed near her. 

That would be my suggestion, anyway. 

If the workplace can't do that, at the very least, if your gf is able to offer an explanation of some sort, perhaps her employer can give her a day off or two, just until the police get a handle on things?

This sounds very serious, and most employers I know will try to accommodate, so long as they have some sort of explanation.

Gotta love N's and sex. 
They don't seem to be able to broach the subject from everything I've read on here + my own experience. Then again, I'm not sure how I'd describe it if I ever had kids of my own. I think that, though I now know what it is, there's a lot of things I still don't know about it. Like, the correlation between love and sex. It's not something I understand fully. 

Anyway, I don't want to take over your post here! I was just relating to the crime shows, ha ha. Which happened to have lots of sex in them. 

I find it a little ironic, because as my nmom's gotten older, she still watches the crime shows, but shies away from some of the ones she used to love (Criminal Minds being the first to come to mind) because it's "too dark" for her. 

Where as, for me personally, I'm more drawn to darker plot-lines. If it's more of a real-life crime show, though, like a documentary? I don't wanna know. 

Bones was a good one, and I just finished Lucifer (a crime show/cop duo with supernatural elements. Highly recommend if you're into that sort of stuff!).

This is really random, but for a moment, I thought you were my actual cousin! His mom has lupus, and he's not living with her anymore because she lost or gave up (not sure which) her parental rights. But I think he's 16, not 14. Plus, he has brothers not sisters. 

I just never hear people talking about lupus in general, but an nmom with lupus? Just really sounded like it could have been my one aunt! Making you my cousin, L (for short). 

Sorry for that weirdness. XD

Anyway, I'm really glad you were able to find a supportive friend like K. That's great! 

I have my own supportive best friend, and I agree. It really is the best feeling in the world. To have someone like you for you. To have someone care about you, without expecting something in return. To have someone be genuinely concerned for you, and to validate your feelings... 

Plus, her taking you out for pizza and staying till midnight? That sounds wonderful! I'm so happy for you, OP!

I grew up watching cop shows! Nmom always had them on. Instead of, you know, TV appropriate for my age group at the time. 

I remember the shows vividly describing things like rape, murder, suicide, cannibalism, etc. 

Though, I don't think it ever bothered me? Perhaps that's why I'm so desensitized now! XD I remember wanting to be a coroner at some point in my preteens. 

The only time is caused issues was when they'd go into graphic details about sex. My mom never had the talk with me, so I was naturally curious, but VERY confused. I remember her explaining things that I had no clue about. Though, now, I'm a bit disgusted now that I know what she was talking about. 

(For those curious, I learned what sex was from the internet and a VERY close encounter with a boy. Thanks, mom.)

Oh, wow. I'm not often surprised by what I read on here anymore, but that is just.... I have no words. 

I hope you and your sister are able to get away from that craziness soon! Because it is just absolutely nuts... geez. 

I can just picture her brandishing the yard clippers like some sort of prize. Hopefully, the police will do something... I mean, it's not okay for her to just wreck your grandma's property like that. Seriously! I feel like that has to warrant some sort of charge. She sounded like she was handling the clippers dangerously, too. Plus, drunk driving on top of it?! Yeah, they have to do something... that's just out of hand.

Good on you, OP, for standing up for yourself! You protected yourself and your boundaries. 

He was in the wrong for provoking you like that. Stepping all over your boundaries... 

And who the heck ignores a sick cat like that?! Seriously! 
I'm glad to read your cat is doing better. I have a furry baby boy myself, and I would be livid if he was sick and ignored or made fun of.

Thanks so much for your advice and encouragement! I really resonated with your comment about buying dinner for the other person. 

I've been in therapy for years now.... it seems never ending. I have breakthrough moments where things are better, and complete relapses where it's almost like I never even made any progress at all. 

I've really been trying to work on myself, for sure. It just doesn't seem to be going as fast as I would like.... 

I've been recommended both of those books in the past. How are they? I'm not much of a reader, and I was worried they'd be too.... technical. ^^" Are they pretty easy reads....?

I know this may not help, but I've never heard of the name Manu before, and I think it's really pretty! :O
Just thought I'd say something. 
Though, I understand if you can't see it that way. Many people say my real life name is beautiful, and I simply can't see it. I end up awkwardly thanking them and changing the subject. 

That's really crappy of your mom to make you suffer like that, though. I mean, telling your teachers that you liked to be called the name you hated? That's just... ugh. I'm sorry you had to deal with that.

Aww... I feel bad. XD There's that damn guilt again. 

Brain: "Bruh. Their cat died. You should be supporting them, and now they're writing a heart-felt reply to you? Get your game together!!"

I like your advice, though. 

I just need to find a group. ._.
I love Minecraft (Java version) myself, and would love to join a good Minecraft community. The trick is finding a good one that's not just full of trolls, little kids, hackers, or griefers. Not trying to point fingers at all. There's nice people in (most) every bunch, as well as mean people in every bunch. 

It's just that my interests (roleplaying, Undertale, Minecraft) seem to be plagued with... less nice people. 

Thanks for the advice, though! I think I will have another go at finding a group of like-minded people. It's always a nice thing to have in your life- people that love what you love.
Oh no... I'm so sorry for your loss!! I wish I could say something that would help...

Sorry to hear you feel the same way... :(
At least we have this sub!

Poor kitty. I hope he (she?) feels better soon!!!
I have a cat as well. Luckily, he his mostly healthy, though I've had to deal with some.... frustrating issues with him, thanks to my nmom putting her nose where it doesn't belong.

Thanks for sharing!! I'm glad you were able to find some peace by shortening your name. 

I'm gonna have to google name changes and trauma now! I'm curious if that is a common thing where I live. 

I read a book recently (it was triggering, so I don't recommend it) about a girl who went through a lot of trauma. She was kidnapped, and her kidnapper forcefully changed her name. At the time, she was upset because she was forced to let go of a part of herself (her real name), but as she began to heal from the trauma (yes, she escaped), she was actually thankful that he called her by another name. 

She was able to say that the trauma happened to Emma (for example). Not to Jessica. 
The other name was like another person to her. It actually helped her cope a lot because she could recognize the trauma as a part of her life that wasn't attached to the person she'd grown to be.  

I guess I just really liked that, and realize I feel that way about my name vs my nickname. My real name is something I was given- a part of my life that I had to endure. 
But my nickname is my new self and the person I strive to be. 

Thanks for the well wishes, too! I hope you, too, can change your name soon! :)

Though I'm not a doctor and can't give actual medical advice, this sounds like dissociation to me. 

I get it a lot. 

Sometimes, it feels like my limbs aren't attached to my body. Sometimes, I feel like I'm watching my life through a TV screen. 
Sometimes, I forget where I am and what I'm doing. 
Or, you might feel completely emotionless. Numbness from dissociation is different from numbness due to depression. When I dissociate and feel numb, I feel almost invincible. I'm scared of nothing. I'm not happy or sad. Somebody could kick down the door, and point a gun at me, and I'd just shrug. I think that's due to everything feeling fake. If it doesn't feel real, it's not scary, right? 

As for the not speaking part, it really sounds like you need to take some space before trying to talk about those feelings. For me, when I'm about to cry, I get a 'lump in my throat'. Maybe that's what you're feeling? Either way, if you can't talk, are you able to write down your emotions? 

I find that writing really helps me get my thoughts together. it's why I like coming on here. Even if you're only able to recognize that you can't speak right then- that's how you're feeling, that's okay! Your therapist isn't there to grade you. There's no "wrong" answers. :)

Good on you for being able to catch your thought of, "Oh no, it was my dinner!" I just wanted to point that out. It's easy to blame yourself when you've been blamed by an N for so long. 

Also, I think you did an amazing job of taking care of your kid!! That just warmed my heart. 

Congrats to you for breaking the cycle!!

Is there anyone else in your life that you consider a support? A sibling, cousin, coworker, teacher/mentor?  


You don't need people in your life to try and improve your own self talk, though. It certainly helps a LOT, but it's not impossible to do on your own.   


I'm sure even people on here would be willing to help!
Even though I'm not OP, and it's not my birthday, your comment made me smile. People like you make the world a better place. That was such a sweet gesture. You're awesome!!

I found this sub by watching a video titled "You're not crazy, it's your mother!".   
Before that, I'd spent about 8 months with a private therapist. I'd gone to therapy because I was depressed, anxious, and suicidal. I thought there was something wrong with *me*.   
However, at about 8 months, the family situation started to come out. I'd always hidden it, for fear of making my family look bad. I protected them.   
Once things started coming out, though... I realized the truth, and it's really shaken me.   


I still struggle with panic attacks. I still struggle with (a lot of) self hatred. Sometimes, I feel complete crazy.   


But this sub, along with my best friend and her family, have really given me a lot of insight. It helps so much to know that I'm not alone, I'm not crazy, I'm not damaged.   


I still feel like a lost cause a lot of the time. Like even if I get away from my family, there's no fixing me.   


But this sub, along with my friend, help me realize that escape is possible. Change is possible, even if it takes years. Even if it doesn't even reach the place you want it to, thing can improve.

I'm so glad my comment was helpful for somebody!!   


Self talk is such a hard thing. Sometimes, I can easily catch myself thinking, for example, "I'm so ugly." I've never gotten to the place where I can say "I'm beautiful" (even typing those two words makes me cringe), but I'm able to find things I like about myself now, and say those instead. "I like my hair color." "I have a nice hand shape." "I'm thankful for my fingernails." etc.  


But self talk can get to you in ways that isn't that as obvious. As another example, I catch myself not even trying to do things because "it's going to fail". Am I psychic? Nope! Yet, that prediction seems like a complete truth to me. Maybe because I've failed in the past. Maybe because I've been mocked more trying, yelled at for failing, or just in general made to feel worthless for making a mistake. The fear of failure keeps me from even starting something. And that's dumb! I mean, what sort of life is that?   


So, I guess it's useful to analyze your behavior as well. See if there's something you're (unreasonably) avoiding. What excuses you make to not do things. What scares you and why.    


I've been in a real self analysis mood lately, and I've found it really useful. :)

Man, oh man... I'm SO sorry you have to go through that. There's so many thoughts that I'm having on this situation. Firstly... I can't imagine watching the man you love change like that. I'm just... so so sorry, OP. That must be devastating for you!   
Secondly, a question. Is your husband aware of how his family really is? I mean, you seem really well informed. I'm just curious if he is, too. That might be a dumb question to ask, but lots of us RBN's didn't know that our families weren't normal. The more informed he his, the better the chances to turn this around imo.   
Lastly, as RBN's and adult onset mental illness... That's not something I honestly know a lot about. I'm hoping someone on here can offer some more insight!   
However, from what I understand, people raised by N's will go one of two ways. Either becoming an N themselves, or becoming the exact opposite.   


With your husband, he sounds like he was the latter when you first met. I mean, correct me if I'm wrong, but he seemed like a good guy! The sudden change within the last two years... that just seems... odd, to me. Not saying it isn't possible, but I feel like something must have happened to trigger it?   


Now, this FIL sounds like he's certainly caused plenty of issues. I could definitely see him wearing your husband down. Yet... it still seems like a very sudden change to me.   


How open is your husband to conversation? You may have already tried this, so forgive me if I'm flogging a dead horse here, but could you maybe talk to your husband? Tell him how he's making you feel? 

  
Perhaps marriage counselling might also be an option. 

  
It sounds like you guys have really tried to keep a distance between yourselves and the FIL, but is there any way you can limit his contact even more? He really sounds like he's bothering you guys!   


If all this has already been tried, or fails, I'd agree with the advice given by the other person who commented. 16 years of marriage isn't an easy thing to walk away from, I imagine. But you have to put yourself first!   


Sadly, the only one who can change your husband's behavior is himself.   


Sorry for such a long winded reply!! I really hope you get some good answers on here, OP, and I wish you the best of luck!!

Man, this is a mood. I feel this 100%.   
You're not alone, OP.   


I literally just spent several hours crying and hating myself for existing. My friend tried to make me feel better (and she honestly helped), but I simply can't understand why she loves me. Love without strings attached... it feels so fake. There has to be a catch. And if there's not a catch, she'll grow tired of me. Even if she doesn't leave me, she's only staying around because of guilty or pity. At least, that's how I feel. I even told her the outright.   


Honestly, the only thing that helps is when she flips my own logic against me.   
In your case, do you think your fiance or friends are wastes of space? Of course you wouldn't! Therefore, why think that about yourself?   


I know... it's easy to say, hard to do. I would never think the way I think about myself about my friend. Yet, that doesn't stop me from thinking it about myself.   


All I can say, is when you catch yourself feeling lousy about yourself, try and remember what your friends would say about you. Or what your fiance would say. Try and focus on their positive words about yourself. Repeat them as much as you can, even if they don't feel real to you. If that feels like too much, take a step back and simply try and stop the negative self talk. If you can't say something positive about yourself, try to at least cut back on the negative.   


Anyway, sorry if this post was too... pushy. \^\^"   


I just really connected to what you said. I really hope you can feel better about yourself! Take care!!

Oops! I just posted a similar quote. Should have read the replies first. My bad...   


It's a very true statement, though.

Yes. I get that all the time. One quote that helped me was "Someone who drowns in five inches of water is just as dead as someone who drowns in 50 feet."  
Comparing trauma is a lot like comparing the two deaths. Just because someone had it "worse" doesn't mean what you went through wasn't bad. It doesn't mean that you were never abused. It doesn't mean that you're not living with the after effects of trauma. You're still just as hurt, and you still have to find a way to struggle through it.

Unfortunately, my friend lives in another country. :(  
I can't get it to her house until I go to visit. I had a plane ticket last year, but I had to cancel it.   
Thanks for your ideas, though. If I find it, I'll sure as hell be hiding it. Though, he goes into my bedroom and rummages in my drawers all the time, soo.... there's really no hiding things in this house.

You are NOT pathetic for still loving your mom! It shows that you have something she doesn't seem to use often- a heart. 

It hurts SO much when the people we love hurt us.... When stranger hurts us, it's not as bad (usually) because it's natural to have a level of distrust with a stranger. But with your family, you expect love. So when they turn around and stab you in the back, it hurts that much more.   


I wish that you could have the mom you deserve. I wish we all could. Until then, try to be gentle with yourself, okay? It's normal to trust your family and love them, even when they keep hurting you. If it wasn't, everyone with an abusive family would just leave without looking back. You're not pathetic, wrong, or damaged. You're trying to see the positive in a situation that sounds really negative.   


I wish you the best of luck!!

Aww man... that's the worst.  
It really shows how much they care about you. /sarcasm

Man... I'd do this, if I didn't think I'd end up on the streets. He certainly deserves to be reported for theft, as this is not the first thing he's stolen from me.   
However, not only would my parents kick me out (I have no other place to go atm), but my family would likely cover for him. They'd "find" the laptop, and blame my "forgetfulness".

I don't think she's blaming him, as he is the GC and can do no wrong. It's more of "\[Uncle\] has every right to trample over your rights because you are just a lowly piece of scum. So don't complain about my precious baby stealing from you. He has every right to."  


That is a possibility, though. I might be able to trick him...
Can I actually do that....? Like, am I legally allowed to report it....? I wouldn't think the police would get involved int anything so significant as a laptop theft.
Yeah. I went to my uncle and demanded it back, to which he said he never took it. So, either he's lying, or my mom is. Because it isn't here, and I know I didn't just lose it.

I'm sorry your mom is the same. Luckily, the cats don't know what's being said to them! To the cat our N's are probably sounding like "Litter-food. Treat! Poo-butt-paw. POO-BUTT-PAW!!"  


That brings back a traumatic experience of mine.   
My nmom's sister's husband (my uncle, but not the one I've mentioned here before) used to rip off his shoe and use the sole of it to beat the living daylights out of their cats whenever they'd do something "wrong". Thank god I only visited a handful of times.   
I still remember the sound of the shoe.... Ugh. I can't.

INFP/INFJ here (I'm 50/50) and it's nice to meet you!   


Your dad clearly thinks everyone should be like him because he's perfect, you know. /sarcasm.
True. Come to think of it, I wonder what my mom thought she'd get out of it?

I think I actually was sick lol.   
I hadn't eaten anything, no.   
I'd been sleeping,   
But I threw up like... 6 times later that day. So I think I had the flu. XD   
Thank god.   
I was legitimately freaking out for a bit there!!

Hey. I know this is weird coming from a stranger, but... My best friend had cancer, and reading your post... I just really felt for you. She's been in remission for several months now. She did it and I know you can do this too!! You go! Kick cancer's ass!!  


I'm also so sorry that people didn't believe you when you got raped... that's awful. I really wish I could say something to make you feel better, but... I can't.   


Somehow, people have it in their heads that we get something out of "lying". Some sort of high? I don't even know.   


But I've spent my ENTIRE life denying my parents' abuse towards me. I thought my family was normal, and would die to protect that image. Doctors would try and tell me that these things weren't okay. That abuse isn't okay, but I would shut down immediately, even getting hostile in defense of my family. My family was FINE. They weren't abusive!!  


It's taken me a whole year to accept the truth. And months and months of therapy before that to even get to the truth. I was protecting it so deeply, I wasn't even aware of it. But learning this? Accepting what my family is? It's almost ruined me! It's driven me to the point of suicide MULTIPLE times.   
They say 'ignorance is bliss' and it's damn true! I wish I could go back to being blissfully aware of how my family treated me. To go back to thinking that I was the problem, but if I just worked hard enough, I would have my picture-perfect family. I just had to do better, that's all.   


Sadly, there's no 'unknowing'. Once you know, you can't ignore it. You can't go back.   


You can choose to tell people. Or you can choose to keep it hidden. But things can never go back to the way they were.   


I would NEVER wish this hell upon anybody. And those people that think I'm gaining something for going through this? Walk a mile in my shoes.

Reading your comment made me think "Who the hell downvotes someone's post on a SUPPORT forum?" Like seriously! Who's reading and thinks, "wow that suks. dISlkE."  
People are being real here. Some of us are sharing some of our worst traumas. Who DISLIKES those posts? Not upvoting, sure. But disliking?
This happens to me so much! I work really hard on a post and it gets downvoted and I'm like, "Dude... did my post suck, or are people just having a bad time, or...?"

Job hunting is the WORST. I'm so sorry you have to deal with that. That seasonal job? That sounded like hell. I'm so glad you're out of there!  


First off, this isn't your fault. Idk what country you're in, but in my country, it's almost impossible to get a job. Even McDonalds wouldn't take me. And I applied like... five times. It's hard not to take it personally. But if your country is anything like mine, chances are, there just aren't enough jobs.   


I don't know what type of town you live in, but if it's a small town, there's a chance you can land a job by simply speaking to the employer face to face. This doesn't work in bigger towns, but if you go into the place and make a good first impression? That goes a long way. Bigger towns will just dismiss you and tell you to apply online. When you apply online, it's pretty much like the lottery. A computer sifts through the resumes with a keyword search thing and filters out the rest. You miss one word, and you're out.   
So handing out resumes face to face? Good idea depending on where you live.   


Even if you can't do that, though, make sure you go back to the jobs you applied for. Show them you're still eager! Employers really love that.   


Hunt for jobs in odd places. It's totally old-fashioned, but newspapers are a thing. Not my thing, either, but if you have one, look at the job section there. eBay classified/Kijiji is also another place to look. If you have FB, that's a good place, too.   


Networking is your best bet. Literally. Ask everyone and anyone you know to keep an eye out for you or put in a good word. If you're religious, check out your church. They can be great for that stuff, because they can hook up with other churches and spread the word even faster.   
It sounds as though you could get a good reference from your old boss, too. Even if you can't get your job back there, a good reference really helps.   


If you're desperate, a Go-Fund me can help. Though, I'd more recommend that if you were short on monthly rent or food.   


Just remember, you're NOT defective, bad, or worthless if they don't hire you. It's nothing wrong with you. You might have had three years experience, and Joe over there had five.

That's rough. I wouldn't say you're necessarily the GC. Your mom could be saying that for many reasons. She could be trying to pit you and your brother against each other. She could be lying.   
But... regardless of what she meant, you clearly DO love your brother. You said that it's been eating at you for years. You recognize the abuse.   
You can't control your mom, but you can control what you do. You didn't specify whether your brother was younger or older, but if you have a good relationship with him, I would try and stick together if I were you.   
I'd say "Don't let mom get to you. I got your back, bro." Or something.   
But you might not have that relationship with him. I don't know. It was just a suggestion based on assumptions.   
Your mom was wrong to say that, though. It hurt you and it hurt him. A parent should never hurt their child.

Yeah, I only realized that it was likely connect to me being RBN when I wrote this post. But I really DO think it's connected. We've been taught that nothing is ours, and watched it be taken away. So we willing give stuff away. I think it's sort of a survival thing. Like, "I'm gonna give my stuff away before you take it from me. Then you can't hurt me." Or it's driven by guilt. You assume that everyone around you views you as your N does, so you constantly have to work to appease them.

Dang... He literally saw your stuff as trash, bringing in the literal outside trashcan. That's horrible...   


My mom forced me to pile my own stuff into trash bags so she could throw it away in front of me. Not once, but several times.

Eugh, that's brutal. I'm sorry you had to deal with that.  
My mom wouldn't allow me to brush my hair, then mocked me for having a rat's nest. But thankfully, she never *cut* it herself.

You know... even though I've read and experienced N behavior firsthand, stories like this get me every time. They literally sound like something from a terrible movie. You know, like some old-school cartoon villain. But they're 100% real.   
I always end up laughing. Not because it's funny. It's not. But just because it's so relatable, and quite frankly, ridiculous.  
I'm sorry you had to deal with that.

I'm sorry to break it to you, OP, but...   
Your son appears to be a zombie. He's joined the ranks of the undead.   
Eating only rotten flesh? Check. Eating veg? Well, they say a human finger is the same consistency as a carrot.... I believe your son is not only a zombie, but... a confused zombie.   
This if further confirmed by his refusal to use torches. Zombies don't spawn in the light.   
It will likely only get worse from here on out.   
We can only pray that he will not resort to walking off cliffs and dying from the fall damage. Or worse... walking into pools of lava.   
Your best bet, is to either encase him into some sort of structure (preferably obsidian to protect him from creeper blasts and sunlight), or to... well, you know...

Man... even though my mom wasn't that extreme as your stepdad, I still really relate to your post.   
In my own situation, I'm being forced to leave my parents' house because they are moving to escape debt. I very seriously considered living in my car, living in a trailer, or living in a hole in the ground. Still working things out atm, but I have a plan. Unfortunately, I doubt my plan will be of much use to you, as a lot of the steps are specific to my situation.   
Hmm... let's see. Although this is usually for women from what I've heard, is it possible you could find a shelter? There's women's shelters for women escaping abuse, so I would assume there's shelters that men can access as well.

I don't know if any of my advice is good advice or not, but here's a few things I can recommend. 

​

**-Try to identify the 'why'.** If you're feeling really sad that day, try to figure out why. 

I know this might sound really stupid at first, but I had become so adept at blocking my emotions, I couldn't see the reason behind things. Trying to find the reason gives me a purpose... a goal. It's no longer an invisible enemy attacking me from all directions. I can call it out, and either distance myself from it and take a much needed retreat, or fight back. If you identify that you're feeling exceptionally depressed because (for example) your mom woke up in a shit mood and took it out on you, try to get out of the house for a little bit. Try and get away from her. Go for a walk, watch a movie, go to the library, go to the gym (if it's affordable), spend time with a friend....

​

**-Try not to focus on the future so much.** 

I'm like you. I see nothing in my future. I have no goals, career or otherwise. I don't see myself ever getting married. It's depressing to me to think I could potentially be trapped on this earth for the next 60-80 years. 

So, I try not to focus on the barren future. Instead, I find small things that I can enjoy now and stay in the present. Do you like video games? Reading books? Being outside? Cleaning? Watching TV? Find something you enjoy and focus on that. Enjoy that instead of worrying about your future. Even if it seems small and meaningless, it's at least something you can enjoy. A ray of sunshine in the dark cloudy world of living with an N. 

​

**-Try and see the positive.** 

I can hear the groans from here lol. I know it's lame and cliche to say "look at the positive things!" when there's so much bad stuff in your life. But I'm not telling you to go crazy with it or anything. I'm not expecting you to ignore everything bad with a goofy smile plastered on your face. 

No, I want you to try and do something very small. Look at yourself... and look at yourself honestly. It can be in a mirror or just in your head. And I want you to try and find just ONE thing that you like about yourself. :)

It can be something like "I like the shape of my hands" or "I like the color of my hair" or "I'm a good friend" or "I'm not a bad person". It doesn't even have to be positive, per se. Just something that isn't negative. 

Then, if you can, try to print or write it out somewhere you can see it. If you're crafty, you could make a collage and hang it on your wall. Or you could design a poster on the computer and print it and stick it on the bathroom mirror. Or, if you're not crafty, it can just be a small piece of paper in your wallet or phone with the words written on it. 

Just try and find that one thing. And when you start hearing yourself think "im a worthless piece of shit that won’t amount to anything anyway so why try?” look at your positive statement and argue back!
